rules: Output is always `String(count) + "\n"` on stdout, exit 0. Any Python exception => exit 1, stdout EMPTY (no partial count). Malformed JSON in --a/--b also exits 1 (json.decoder.JSONDecodeError), NOT exit 2.

`format` is COMPLETELY INERT: no format_checker is installed, so every format name with every invalid value yields 0 errors. Confirmed for email, date-time, uri, regex("["), plus (in earlier runs) date, time, ipv4, ipv6, hostname, json-pointer, uuid, idn-email. An unknown format name yields 0. A non-string format value (5) or an object value ({"type":"integer"}) yields 0 with no exception. {"type":"string","format":"email"} on instance 1 => 1 (only type counts).

`contentEncoding`, `contentMediaType`, `contentSchema` are NOT keywords: base64 garbage => 0, "application/json" with "{not json" => 0, contentSchema:{type:integer} on a JSON-string => 0, wrong-typed values (contentEncoding:123, contentMediaType:false) => 0.

Annotations are fully inert even when holding broken subschemas or wrong types: title/description/default/examples/$comment/readOnly/writeOnly/deprecated all yield 0. {"default":{"type":"string"}} => 0; {"$comment":{"required":true}} nested under properties => 0; {"examples":[{"$ref":"#/nope"}],"default":{"$ref":"#/nope"}} => 0 (never resolved). All 8 annotations plus type:integer on "x" => exactly 1.

Keywords from other drafts that Draft7 IGNORES (verified individually, each with a type-appropriate instance so the keyword would have fired if implemented): dependentRequired, dependentSchemas, prefixItems, unevaluatedItems, unevaluatedProperties, minContains, maxContains, contentSchema, $defs, $anchor, $recursiveRef, $recursiveAnchor, $dynamicRef, $dynamicAnchor, $vocabulary, divisibleBy (draft3), disallow (draft3), extends (draft3), id (draft4), nullable (OpenAPI). All yield 0.

`$defs` and `definitions` are inert AS KEYWORDS but are still reachable by JSON pointer: {"$defs":{"x":false},"$ref":"#/$defs/x"} => 1 and {"definitions":{"x":false},"$ref":"#/definitions/x"} => 1. Subschemas inside them are never *visited*, so junk there is harmless: {"definitions":{"x":{"$schema":[]}}} => 0, {"$defs":{"x":{"$ref":"#/nope"}}} => 0, {"foo":{"$id":5}} => 0.
`then` / `else` alone (no `if`) are ignored => 0. {"if":{"type":"integer"},"then":false} => 1 (control).
`additionalItems` is inert when `items` is a schema rather than an array: {"items":{"type":"integer"},"additionalItems":false} on [1,2] => 0.

Unknown keywords are ignored regardless of key shape or value: "foo", "$$x", "0", "" (empty string), non-ASCII "ты", "type�" all => 0, even when the value is false / a broken subschema / [1,2] / null.

Keyword matching is EXACT and case-sensitive with no trimming: "Type", "TYPE", "tYpe", " type", "type ", "properties ", "maximum " (nested), "Properties", "REQUIRED", "AllOf", "ANYOF", "Enum", "NOT", "Items", "IF", "Then" are ALL inert => 0.

`$schema` AT THE ROOT is entirely ignored (the script hard-codes Draft7Validator): draft3/draft4/draft6/2019-09/2020-12/"garbage"/5/null/[]/{"a":1} all leave draft7 semantics and never throw. {"$schema":"...draft-03...","divisibleBy":3} on 5 => 0; {"$schema":"...draft-04...","minimum":3,"exclusiveMinimum":true} on 3 => 0; {"$schema":"...2020-12...","prefixItems":[{"type":"string"}]} on [1] => 0.

BIG ONE: `$schema` inside a SUBSCHEMA DOES switch the validator class for that subschema and everything below it. {"allOf":[{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","prefixItems":[{"type":"string"}]}]} on [1] => 1. Also validating in switched subschemas: 2020 items-as-schema, 2020 maxContains, 2020 unevaluatedProperties, 2019 dependentRequired, draft4 boolean exclusiveMinimum, draft3 divisibleBy/disallow/extends/union-type/property-level required:true. Same switch happens under `properties`, `not`, `patternProperties`, and is INHERITED by deeper subschemas that have no $schema of their own.

Root `$schema` does NOT propagate down: {"$schema":"...2020-12","allOf":[{"prefixItems":[{"type":"string"}]}]} on [1] => 0. Only a $schema physically present in a subschema switches the class (and then the switched class is inherited downward).

$schema URI recognition: the string is normalized only by urlsplit/urlunsplit — the SCHEME is lower-cased and an EMPTY trailing fragment is dropped; nothing else. Recognized: http://json-schema.org/draft-0{3,4,6,7}/schema with or without trailing '#', https://json-schema.org/draft/{2019-09,2020-12}/schema with or without trailing '#', and HTTP:// (uppercase scheme). NOT recognized (silently falls back to the parent's class, no warning, no error): uppercase HOST, https:// for draft-04, http:// for 2020-12, non-empty fragment ('...schema#/definitions/x'), '...schema##', '...schema/', '...schema ' (trailing space), 'garbage', 'http://json-schema.org/schema#', and null.

Non-string $schema in a SUBSCHEMA CRASHES (contrast with root, where it is ignored): 5 => AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'decode'; true => 'bool' ... 'decode'; 1.5 => 'float' ... 'decode'; [] => TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'; {} => TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'. null is the only non-string that is safe (falls back). This only fires when the subschema is actually visited: {"patternProperties":{"^a$":{"$schema":[]}}} => exit 1 with instance {"a":1} but => 0 with instance {}.

draft4-style BOOLEAN exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum are NOT ignored — draft7 treats them as NUMBERS via Python bool==int: {"exclusiveMaximum":true} => 1 error for instance 5 and for 1, 0 errors for 0; {"exclusiveMaximum":false} => 1 for 0, 0 for -1; {"exclusiveMinimum":true} => 1 for 0, 0 for 2; {"minimum":3,"exclusiveMinimum":true} => 2 errors for instance 0 (both keywords fire) and 0 errors for instance 3. Boolean or string instances are skipped (not type number) => 0. Same coercion for {"minimum":true} on 0 => 1, {"maxLength":true} on "ab" => 1, {"multipleOf":true} on 5 => 0.

draft3-style `required` as a BOOLEAN is not ignored — it CRASHES in draft7 because the implementation iterates the value: {"required":true} or {"required":false} or {"required":5} with an OBJECT instance => exit 1 (TypeError: 'bool'/'int' object is not iterable). With a non-object instance it short-circuits => 0. Under properties: {"properties":{"a":{"required":true}}} => exit 1 for {"a":{}} but 0 for {"a":1} (the property value must be an object to reach the crash).

`required` with other container types iterates them: {"required":"ab"} on {} => 2 errors (one per CHARACTER); {"required":{"a":1,"b":2}} on {} => 2 errors (one per KEY); {"required":[1]} on {} => 1 error (non-string member, no exception); {"required":[]} => 0.

$ref sibling suppression: when a schema object contains `$ref`, ALL other keywords in that same object are skipped — and this is governed by the draft of the PARENT that descends into it, not by the object's own $schema. {"definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/x","type":"integer"} => 1 on instance 1 and 0 on instance "s". A crash-triggering sibling is never even evaluated: {"$ref":"#/definitions/x","required":true,"definitions":{"x":true}} on {} => 0.

Corollary that will bite: a 2020-12 subschema that is reached FROM a draft7 parent still has its $ref siblings suppressed ({"$defs":{"x":true},"allOf":[{"$schema":"...2020-12","$ref":"#/$defs/x","minimum":100}]} on 1 => 0), but one level deeper — where the parent is now the 2020 class — siblings DO apply ({...,"allOf":[{"$schema":"...2020-12","allOf":[{"$ref":"#/$defs/x","minimum":100}]}]} => 1, and with $defs.x=false => 2 errors). Draft7-parented equivalent => 1.

`$id` must be a string in any VISITED schema object: {"$id":5} at root => exit 1 (AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'startswith'); {"$id":[]} => 'list' ... 'startswith'; {"properties":{"a":{"$id":5}}} => exit 1 for {"a":1} but 0 for instance 1. draft4-style {"id":5} is always safe => 0.

The resource identifier is read with the PARENT's specification, not the subschema's $schema: {"allOf":[{"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#","$id":5}]} => exit 1 (draft7 parent reads $id) while {"allOf":[{"$schema":"...draft-04...","id":5}]} => 0.

Draft7 id_of skips `$id` entirely when `$ref` is present in the same object: {"$ref":"#","$id":5} does NOT raise the $id AttributeError — it raises RecursionError instead (self-reference), and {"$id":"http://ex.com/s","$ref":"#/definitions/x","definitions":{"x":false}} => 1.
`enum` members and `const` values are DATA, not schemas: {"enum":[{"$schema":[]}]} on 1 => 1 (no crash), {"const":{"required":true}} on 1 => 1 (no crash).

Root schema must be an object or a boolean. true => 0, false => 1, {} => 0. Anything else exits 1: 5 / 1.5 => TypeError: argument of type 'int'/'float' is not iterable; null => TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable; "x" and even "$ref" => AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'; [], [{"type":"string"}], ["$ref"] => AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'. Same shape of failure for non-object subschemas: {"allOf":[5]} => TypeError not iterable; {"properties":{"a":"x"}} on {"a":1} => AttributeError 'str' has no 'get'.

Unresolvable $ref exits 1 (jsonschema.exceptions._WrappedReferencingError: PointerToNowhere), and $ref resolving to a schema with junk $schema also exits 1 when resolved: {"$ref":"#/definitions/x","definitions":{"x":{"$schema":[]}}} => exit 1.

Other broken-value crashes observed in this family: {"multipleOf":false} on 5 => ZeroDivisionError: integer modulo by zero; {"exclusiveMaximum":null} => TypeError '>=' int vs NoneType; {"exclusiveMaximum":"5"} => TypeError '>=' int vs str; {"maxLength":null} on "x" => TypeError '>' int vs NoneType; {"pattern":"["} => re.error only when a STRING instance reaches it (0 for instance 1).
gotchas: Python bool IS an int, so draft4-style boolean exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum become numeric comparisons instead of being ignored or crashing. Proof: --b '{"exclusiveMaximum":true}' --a '5' => 1 (5 >= 1), --a '0' => 0. And --b '{"exclusiveMaximum":false}' --a '0' => 1 (0 >= 0). In JS, `5 >= true` also coerces, but do NOT special-case booleans as 'ignored'; and note {"minimum":true} on 0 => 1, {"maxLength":true} on "ab" => 1, {"multipleOf":true} on 5 => 0.

Bool/number instances are separated: `true` is NOT of JSON-Schema type number here, so --b '{"exclusiveMinimum":true}' --a 'true' => 0 while --a '0' => 1. A naive JS `typeof x === 'number'` check plus truthiness would get this right only if you explicitly exclude booleans from numeric instances.

`required` is implemented as `for prop in requiredValue`, so a string iterates characters and an object iterates keys, while a bool/int throws. --b '{"required":"ab"}' --a '{}' => 2; --b '{"required":{"a":1,"b":2}}' --a '{}' => 2; --b '{"required":true}' --a '{}' => exit 1. JS `for (const p of "ab")` matches the string case, but `for...of` an object throws and `for...of true` throws — you must reproduce exit-1 for bool/number and key-iteration for objects.

The `required` type guard runs BEFORE iteration, so the crash is instance-dependent: --b '{"properties":{"a":{"required":true}}}' --a '{"a":{}}' => exit 1 but --a '{"a":1}' => 0. A JS implementation that validates schema shape eagerly would wrongly throw (or wrongly not throw) here.

`$schema` is ignored at the ROOT but switches the whole validator dialect inside SUBSCHEMAS. --b '{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","prefixItems":[{"type":"string"}]}' --a '[1]' => 0, but --b '{"allOf":[{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","prefixItems":[{"type":"string"}]}]}' --a '[1]' => 1. A draft7-only JS validator that ignores $schema everywhere will silently miss the second.

Non-string `$schema` is harmless at the root but fatal in a subschema, with different exceptions by type. --b '{"$schema":5,"type":"integer"}' --a '"x"' => 1, but --b '{"allOf":[{"$schema":5,"prefixItems":[...]}]}' --a '[1]' => exit 1 (AttributeError ... 'decode'), and --b '{"allOf":[{"$schema":[]}]}' => exit 1 (TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'). null $schema in a subschema is the only safe non-string.

$schema URI matching is byte-exact after urlsplit normalization (scheme lower-cased, EMPTY trailing '#' dropped) — nothing else is canonicalized. --b '{"allOf":[{"$schema":"HTTP://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#","minimum":3,"exclusiveMinimum":true}]}' --a '3' => 1, but --b '{"allOf":[{"$schema":"http://JSON-SCHEMA.ORG/draft-04/schema#",...}]}' --a '3' => 0. A JS `new URL(...).href` normalization lower-cases the host and would wrongly recognize the second.

$ref sibling suppression is decided by the PARENT's dialect, not the object's own $schema — an artifact of jsonschema's descend(). --b '{"$defs":{"x":false},"allOf":[{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","$ref":"#/$defs/x","minimum":100}]}' --a '1' => 1, but pushing the $ref one level deeper so its parent is the 2020 class: '{"$defs":{"x":false},"allOf":[{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","allOf":[{"$ref":"#/$defs/x","minimum":100}]}]}' --a '1' => 2.

The resource id is extracted with the parent's spec, so `$id` is read even inside a draft4/draft3 subschema. --b '{"allOf":[{"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#","$id":5}]}' --a '1' => exit 1 ('int' object has no attribute 'startswith'), while the draft4-correct '{"allOf":[{"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#","id":5}]}' => 0.

Draft7 id_of returns nothing when `$ref` is a sibling, so a bad `$id` is not even read: --b '{"$id":5}' --a '5' => exit 1 (startswith AttributeError) but --b '{"$ref":"#","$id":5}' --a '1' => exit 1 with RecursionError instead. Same string comparison in JS would report the $id error.

Junk is only fatal if the subschema is actually VISITED — Python is lazy per keyword and per instance. --b '{"patternProperties":{"^a$":{"$schema":[]}}}' --a '{"a":1}' => exit 1, --a '{}' => 0. Likewise '{"properties":{"a":{"$id":5}}}': exit 1 for {"a":1}, 0 for 1. A JS implementation that pre-compiles/validates the whole schema tree will diverge.

A non-object, non-boolean schema produces different Python exceptions depending on whether the value supports `in` and `.get`, all exit 1 with empty stdout: 5/1.5/null => TypeError 'not iterable'; "x" and "$ref" => AttributeError 'str' has no 'get'; []/["$ref"]/[{...}] => AttributeError 'list' has no 'get'. JS `'$ref' in 5` throws too but `'$ref' in []` is false and `[].get` is undefined — you must force exit 1 for every non-object/non-boolean schema.

`format` never validates and never throws, even for values that are not strings — do NOT wire up a format checker or a format-value type check. --b '{"format":"regex"}' --a '"["' => 0 and --b '{"format":5}' --a '"x"' => 0, while a real invalid regex in `pattern` DOES throw: --b '{"pattern":"["}' --a '"a"' => exit 1 (re.error), --a '1' => 0. Python `re` and JS RegExp also disagree on which patterns are invalid ('[' throws in both, but e.g. JS accepts some Python-invalid patterns).

Broken values under IGNORED keywords are never touched, so they must not be schema-checked: --b '{"additionalProperties":false,"prefixItems":[false],"$recursiveRef":"#/nope","$dynamicRef":"#nope","minContains":3,"divisibleBy":0,"id":false, ...}' --a '1' => 0, and --b '{"$defs":{"x":{"$ref":"#/nope"}}}' --a '1' => 0 (an eager JS ref-resolution pass would throw).

Keyword lookup is a plain dict hit: any casing or whitespace variation makes the keyword vanish rather than error. --b '{"Type":"string","TYPE":"string","tYpe":"string"}' --a '1' => 0 and --b '{"properties ":{"a":{"type":"integer"}}}' --a '{"a":"x"}' => 0. Do not normalize keys.
Malformed JSON on --a/--b exits 1 (JSONDecodeError), not 2; argparse-level usage errors are the only exit-2 path. --b '{"a":1},' --a '3' => exit 1 with empty stdout.
exceptionCases: --b '{"exclusiveMaximum":null}' --a '1'  (TypeError: '>=' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'NoneType')
--b '{"exclusiveMaximum":"5"}' --a '1'  (TypeError: '>=' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'str')
--b '{"maxLength":null}' --a '"x"'  (TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'NoneType')
--b '{"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-03/schema#","required":true}' --a '{}'  (TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable; root $schema does not rescue it)
--b '{"properties":{"a":{"$id":5}}}' --a '{"a":1}'  (AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'startswith'; same schema with --a '1' => 0)
--b '{"pattern":"["}' --a '"a"'  (re.error: unterminated character set at position 0; same schema with --a '1' => 0)
--b '5' --a '1'  (TypeError: argument of type 'int' is not iterable)
--b 'null' --a '1'  (TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable)
--b '{"allOf":[5]}' --a '1'  (TypeError: argument of type 'int' is not iterable)
--b '{"a":1},' --a '3'  (json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Extra data; malformed CLI JSON => exit 1, not 2)

rules: Resolution uses the MODERN `referencing` engine (NOT legacy RefResolver): failures are _WrappedReferencingError wrapping PointerToNowhere / Unresolvable / NoSuchAnchor / InvalidAnchor. Every resolution failure is an EXCEPTION (exit 1, empty stdout), never a validation error.

$ref SIBLINGS ARE ALWAYS DROPPED. b={"definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/x","type":"boolean"}: a=1 => 1 (NOT 2); a="s" => 0 (proves the sibling was dropped, since type:boolean would fail). Only $ref, $schema and $id matter in a $ref-bearing object.

Sibling dropping is DIALECT-INDEPENDENT — it still happens when the subschema declares $schema 2019-09 or 2020-12: {"definitions":{"x":true},"allOf":[{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","$ref":"#/definitions/x","type":"string","maximum":0}]} vs 1 => 0. Key order irrelevant ($ref last => still 0).
Control proving it is $ref-specific, not a broken 2020-12 dialect: {"allOf":[{"$schema":"...2020-12/schema","maximum":0,"type":"string"}]} vs 1 => 2.

$ref yields the target's errors INDIVIDUALLY, flattened, with no wrapper error. definitions.x={"required":["a"],"minProperties":2}: {"$ref":"#/definitions/x"} vs {} => 2; that target under items with [{},{}] => 4; reached via ref->ref chain => 2; under additionalProperties with {"a":1,"b":2} => 2; anyOf inside the target still collapses to 1.
Counts compose additively: {"definitions":{"x":{"required":["b"],"minProperties":1}},"properties":{"a":{"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}},"required":["z"]} vs {"a":{}} => 3. Same $ref twice in allOf => 2.
$ref works inside items, properties, additionalProperties, allOf, not, if/then, dependencies, propertyNames. $ref to true => 0, to false => 1, to {} => 0.
Local pointers resolve against the ROOT document (the whole --b value) from any depth, unless an intervening $id changed the base.

Pointer resolution is a generic JSON-Pointer walk: into arrays (#/allOf/0 => 1, #/allOf/1 => 0 for allOf:[{type:string},{type:integer}] vs 1), into arrays under UNKNOWN keywords (#/x/0), into nested definitions (#/definitions/x/definitions/y), and to non-schema containers (#/definitions returns the definitions map, validated as a schema of all-unknown keys => 0).

A pointer target that is not an object or a boolean => EXCEPTION: string => AttributeError 'str' has no attribute 'get'; int => TypeError argument of type 'int' is not iterable; null => TypeError NoneType; array => AttributeError 'list' has no attribute 'get'. Holds at every position (#/type, #/required, #/definitions/x, unknown keys).
Walking THROUGH a segment whose value is an array also throws before later segments apply: {"definitions":{"x":[{...},{...}]},"$ref":"#/definitions/x/1"} => AttributeError 'list' (the /1 never runs).
Pointer escapes use RFC 6901 order (~1 -> '/' first, then ~0 -> '~'): key 'a/b' via #/definitions/a~1b => 1; 'a~b' via a~0b => 1; with BOTH 'a~1b' and 'a/b' present, a~01b resolves to 'a~1b' => 1.

The fragment is PERCENT-DECODED ONCE over the WHOLE fragment BEFORE splitting on '/': %20 finds key 'a b' => 1; %25 -> '%'; %7E0 -> '~0' -> '~' (percent decode precedes ~-unescaping); %2520 finds the literal key 'a%20b' => 1; %2F becomes a real separator, so #/definitions/a%2Fb does NOT find key 'a/b' (PointerToNowhere) but DOES address definitions/a/b => 1.
A raw space is legal in $ref and matches key 'a b' => 1. '+' is NOT decoded to space (matches only a literal 'a+b' key). Trailing whitespace in a pointer is significant.

Array indices are parsed with Python int(): '-1' = LAST element (allOf:[{type:string},{type:integer}] vs 1 => 0), '-2' = first (=> 1); '00' => 0; '+1', ' 1\t' (%201%09) and the FULLWIDTH digit '１' all => index 1; '1_0' => 10; '1.0' and 'x' => ValueError exception; out-of-range (5, -3, or 1_0 with 2 elements) => PointerToNowhere exception.

Python strings are Sequences, so a numeric segment indexes INTO a string value: {"x":"abc"} with #/x/9 => PointerToNowhere, #/x/z => ValueError, #/x/1 => resolves to "b" then throws AttributeError as a non-schema target.

Missing target => PointerToNowhere (#/definitions/nope, #/a/b/c, #//definitions/x whose empty first segment misses). $ref with no leading '#' ('/definitions/x', 'other.json', ' ') => Unresolvable, and NO network fetch is attempted. Non-string $ref => AttributeError 'int' has no attribute 'startswith'.
A fragment that is neither empty, nor '/'-prefixed, nor a registered plain-name anchor => InvalidAnchor exception ('#definitions/x').

Refs that re-enter without consuming instance => RecursionError exception: {"$ref":"#"}, {"$ref":""}, {"allOf":[{"$ref":"#"}]}, mutual definitions a->b->a, {"$id":"http://ex.com/a","allOf":[{"$ref":"http://ex.com/a"}]}.

Recursion that consumes instance is fine: self-recursive definition over a linked list => 0; mutual a->b->a with {"next":{"next":{}}} where b has required:[z] => 1; {"properties":{"a":{"$ref":"#"}},"required":["a"]} vs {"a":{}} => 1; a depth-40 chain => 0.

Root $id registers the root document under that URI so absolute self-refs work: {"$id":"http://ex.com/a","definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"allOf":[{"$ref":"http://ex.com/a#/definitions/x"}]} => 1.

DRAFT-7 LEGACY id_of: $id is IGNORED whenever the SAME object also has a $ref, and when it is fragment-only ('#anch'). So {"$id":"http://ex.com/a","$ref":"http://ex.com/a#/definitions/x","definitions":{...}} => Unresolvable (root never registered under that URI) while the same with $ref:"#/definitions/x" => 1; and {"allOf":[{"$id":"foo.json","$ref":"#/definitions/x"}]} resolves against the ROOT => 1, whereas {"allOf":[{"$id":"foo.json","allOf":[{"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}]}]} => PointerToNowhere because there the base URI did change.

Subschema $id registers a subresource: absolute ('http://ex.com/sub' => 1), relative resolved against the parent base ('sub.json' under root $id http://ex.com/root => 1), and dot-segment ('./sub' under http://ex.com/d/root => 1). A new base plus its own definitions shadows the root's: {"$id":"foo.json","definitions":{"x":{"type":"integer"}},"allOf":[{"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}]} => 0. urn: bases work.
URIs are NOT case-normalized: $ref 'HTTP://EX.COM/sub' against $id 'http://ex.com/sub' => Unresolvable exception.
Draft-4-style "id" is never honored, even inside a subschema declaring $schema draft-04: root {"id":"http://ex.com/a"} + $ref to that URI => Unresolvable exception.

Plain-name anchors: draft7 declares them via $id:"#xa" ({"definitions":{"x":{"$id":"#xa","type":"string"}},"$ref":"#xa"} => 1). $anchor is NOT a draft7 keyword => NoSuchAnchor exception, but it works once that subschema sets $schema 2020-12 => 1.
ROOT $schema IS IGNORED (Draft7Validator is constructed explicitly): {"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#","const":5} vs 1 => 1 (draft7 const still applies).

$schema in ANY SUBSCHEMA DOES switch the dialect for that subschema and everything below: draft-04 subschema ignores const ({"properties":{"p":{"$schema":draft4,"const":5}}} vs {"p":1} => 0) and uses boolean exclusiveMaximum ({"$schema":draft4,"maximum":5,"exclusiveMaximum":true} vs {"p":3} => 0 while the same without $schema => 1); 2019-09 subschema honors dependentRequired ({"a":1} => 1 vs 0 for draft7); 2020-12 subschema honors prefixItems ({"a":[1]} => 1 vs 0).

The switched dialect propagates DOWN into nested subschemas AND THROUGH $ref into the resolved target: {"allOf":[{"$schema":"...2020-12/schema","$ref":"#/definitions/x"}],"definitions":{"x":{"prefixItems":[{"type":"string"}]}}} vs [1] => 1; control without $schema => 0.

An UNRECOGNIZED $schema silently falls back to the CURRENTLY ACTIVE dialect (not draft7, not latest): 'bogus://x' nested inside a 2020-12 subschema still honors prefixItems => 1; 'http://json-schema.org/schema#' (latest alias) and draft-03 at draft7 level keep draft7 (dependentRequired ignored, only maximum fires => 1).
A non-string $schema => AttributeError 'int' object has no attribute 'decode' (exception).

Meta-schemas are BUNDLED offline: {"$ref":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"} vs 1 => 1 (fails the meta-schema's type:[object,boolean]); vs {"type":123} => 1; draft-04 meta => 1; {"allOf":[{"$ref":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"}]} vs 1 => 8 (its own type check + the 7 vocabulary subschemas it $refs). Any OTHER remote/relative URI => Unresolvable exception.

definitions/$defs subschemas are never evaluated unless referenced: {"definitions":{"bad":{"type":"nonsense"}},"type":"integer"} vs 1 => 0; {"definitions":{"bad":{"$ref":"#/nope"}},"type":"integer"} => 0. Referencing the broken one raises jsonschema.exceptions.UnknownType.
gotchas: Array-index segments go through Python int(), which accepts far more than /^\d+$/. NEGATIVE INDICES WRAP: b={"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"integer"}],"$ref":"#/allOf/-1"} a=1 => 0 (last element), "#/allOf/-2" => 1 (first element). Naive JS arr["-1"] is undefined -> you would report not-found.

int() also accepts leading zeros ('#/allOf/00' => index 0 => 1), a leading plus ('#/allOf/%2B1' => index 1 => 0), surrounding ASCII whitespace ('#/allOf/%201%09' => index 1 => 0), UNICODE DIGITS ('#/allOf/１' with U+FF11 => index 1 => 0) and UNDERSCORE SEPARATORS ('#/allOf/1_0' == 10, so with 11 elements => 0 and with 2 elements => PointerToNowhere). But it rejects '1.0' and 'x' with a ValueError EXCEPTION (exit 1), which is a DIFFERENT outcome from the not-found PointerToNowhere exception.

Percent-decoding is applied ONCE to the ENTIRE fragment BEFORE splitting on '/', so %2F creates a new segment: b={"definitions":{"a/b":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a%2Fb"} => EXCEPTION (PointerToNowhere), while b={"definitions":{"a":{"b":{"type":"string"}}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a%2Fb"} => 1. JS code that splits first and decodeURIComponent()s each segment gets both cases backwards.

Python's urllib unquote LEAVES MALFORMED ESCAPES ALONE; JS decodeURIComponent THROWS URIError. b={"definitions":{"a%zzb":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a%zzb"} => 1 (resolves). A JS port must implement a tolerant %XX decoder (and it must be UTF-8 aware: '#/definitions/%C3%A9' finds key 'é' => 1).

unquote does NOT treat '+' as a space (unlike form decoding, and unlike some JS URL helpers). b={"definitions":{"a b":{...}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a+b"} => EXCEPTION, while b={"definitions":{"a+b":{...}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a+b"} => 1.

~-unescaping happens AFTER percent-decoding and only in the RFC 6901 order (~1 then ~0): b={"definitions":{"a~b":{"type":"string"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a%7E0b"} => 1 (%7E -> '~', giving '~0', which then becomes '~'). And with both keys present, b={"definitions":{"a~1b":{"type":"string"},"a/b":{"type":"integer"}},"$ref":"#/definitions/a~01b"} a=1 => 1, i.e. it picks 'a~1b', not 'a/b'.

Python strings are indexable Sequences, so a pointer can walk INTO a string value. b={"x":"abc","$ref":"#/x/9"} => PointerToNowhere; b={"x":"abc","$ref":"#/x/z"} => ValueError; b={"x":"abc","$ref":"#/x/1"} => AttributeError (resolved to the character "b", then used as a schema). A JS port indexing only objects/arrays would call all three 'not found'.

Truthiness/type of the pointer TARGET decides the exception flavor, and none of them are validation errors: string target -> AttributeError, int -> TypeError 'not iterable', null -> TypeError NoneType, array -> AttributeError. So a JS port must EXIT NONZERO (not emit a count) for b={"definitions":{"x":5},"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}.

Draft-7's legacy id_of returns None when the object ALSO has a $ref, so $id is silently discarded there. b={"$id":"http://ex.com/a","$ref":"http://ex.com/a#/definitions/x","definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}}} a=1 => EXCEPTION (Unresolvable) even though the URI textually equals the root $id; removing the root $ref (putting it under allOf) makes the same URI resolve => 1.

Correspondingly, a subschema $id is ignored when it sits next to $ref: {"definitions":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"allOf":[{"$id":"foo.json","$ref":"#/definitions/x"}]} => 1 (root-relative), but nesting the ref one level deeper, {"allOf":[{"$id":"foo.json","allOf":[{"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}]}]} => EXCEPTION. Same $id, opposite outcome.

$ref siblings are dropped even when the subschema opts into 2019-09/2020-12 via $schema — the opposite of what those specs say and of what most JS validators (ajv) do. {"definitions":{"x":true},"allOf":[{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","$ref":"#/definitions/x","type":"string","maximum":0}]} a=1 => 0. Do NOT special-case 2019/2020 to apply siblings.

The ROOT $schema is ignored but a SUBSCHEMA $schema is honored — the reverse of the usual assumption. a=1 b={"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#","const":5} => 1 (draft7 const runs), yet a={"p":1} b={"properties":{"p":{"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#","const":5}}} => 0. A JS port must implement per-subschema dialect switching (draft4/6/7/2019-09/2020-12 keyword tables) and must inherit the active dialect for unknown $schema values.

Meta-schemas resolve OFFLINE from a bundled registry, so remote refs are not uniformly fatal. a=1 b={"allOf":[{"$ref":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"}]} => 8 (not an error, not 1); b={"$ref":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"} => 1; but b={"$ref":"other.json"} => EXCEPTION. Hard-coding 'any absolute URI throws' is wrong.

Unbounded ref recursion becomes a CPython RecursionError (exit 1), not a hang and not a cycle-detection error: b={"$ref":"#"} and b={"$ref":""} both exit 1. There is also a DEPTH LIMIT on legitimate recursion: for schema {"definitions":{"n":{"properties":{"next":{"$ref":"#/definitions/n"}}}},"$ref":"#/definitions/n"} a linked list of depth 246 => 0 but depth 248 => exit 1 (RecursionError); the boundary drops to ~200 when an anyOf is added per level, so it is frame-count dependent, not a fixed schema depth.

"$ref":"" (empty string) and "$ref":"#" behave identically (both resolve to the root), whereas "$ref":"/definitions/x" (no '#') is Unresolvable and "$ref":"#definitions/x" is InvalidAnchor. Three different failure paths for three near-identical strings.
URI comparison is byte-exact: 'HTTP://EX.COM/sub' does not match $id 'http://ex.com/sub' => Unresolvable. JS code using `new URL()` normalizes scheme and host to lowercase and would resolve it.
exceptionCases: --a 1 --b {"definitions":{"x":5},"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}   (TypeError: argument of type 'int' is not iterable)
--a 1 --b {"definitions":{"x":null},"$ref":"#/definitions/x"}   (TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable)

NOT in the corpus but observed: a linked list of depth 248 against {"definitions":{"n":{"properties":{"next":{"$ref":"#/definitions/n"}}}},"$ref":"#/definitions/n"} exits 1 with RecursionError (depth 246 => 0).
